name: Arc III: The Spire of Lore and Doom

pages.name: Arc III Overview: The Spire of Lore and Doom
pages.html:
Levels 8–12 · default 16 sessions · expandable to 18. Palanthas becomes the campaign’s first true urban sandbox before the cursed Tower becomes a multi-session megadungeon.

The party remains in Palanthas after the Shoikan Grove recognises Raistlin’s token. They are now watched by every faction that understands even a fraction of what happened. The city calls them the Hands of Wayreth; some say the Black Master’s Hands.

Arc Structure

SessionsPhaseResult
1–3Palanthas investigationFistandantilus trail; the Long Return named
4–5Shoikan GroveParty reaches subordinate entrance
6–10Upper/middle TowerHistory, Orders, Caramon revelation, Garden Incident
11–15Deep TowerRannoch, Fistandantilus, possible futures, necromantic proof, lower seals
16Portal and MasterRaistlin arrives; Master of Past and Present; Level 12

The Tower is not simply twelve floors. Published lore describes a vast 33-floor structure with a hollow core and a spiral stair climbing through it. For table play, treat the twelve named adventure zones as the meaningful floors/complexes. Between them are sealed residences, empty archives, collapsed landings and duplicate service levels that preserve the Tower’s impossible scale without requiring thirty-three maps.

Arc Question

Can knowledge be recovered without becoming its old owner? The party spends the arc learning exactly what Fistandantilus discovered and exactly why Raistlin is capable of finishing it.

pages.name: Palanthas Sandbox Operations
pages.html:
Palanthas should remain alive around the dungeon. The party may leave the Grove, consult the Library, bargain with factions and return with new plans.

Three Clocks

ClockAdvance WhenAt 4
Veyrath CellThe party makes a public move or leaves evidence unsecuredEnemy agents attempt entry to the Tower behind them
Palanthas AlarmUndead incidents, Grove disturbances or public magic occurCouncil considers sealing the district and arresting collaborators
Raistlin ArrivalMajor Tower recognition events are reportedRaistlin comes personally; normally held until Session 16

Downtime Between Delves

One night in Palanthas can restore resources, research a clue, meet one faction, and allow one clock to move. This makes returning to the city meaningful without removing pressure.

Research Sources

  • Great Library: histories, dates, copies, chronicled public events.
  • University: magical theories, architectural plans, scholarly rivalry.
  • Order contacts: secret doctrine, spell provenance, political context.
  • Old City: physical evidence and forgotten access routes.
  • Harbour: intelligence, smuggling, enemy movement.
  • Shoikan district residents: folklore, missing people, what the Grove does rather than why.

Do Not Close the City Too Early

The Tower is the central mystery, but the party should still care about inns, scholars, neighbours and streets. Their later choices during the siege depend on relationships built here.

pages.name: Arc III Factions
pages.html:
Every faction wants the Tower problem solved differently. None should exist merely to obstruct the party.

FactionPublic PositionPrivate Fear
RaistlinRecover dangerous historical knowledge before Takhisis does.That the Tower will reject him—or accept him and prove the path real.
Astinus & AestheticsRecord and preserve.That intervention would create the history they are trying to observe.
Palanthas CouncilKeep citizens safe and the cursed district contained.A second magical sovereign inside their walls.
Knights of SolamniaPrevent an enemy from gaining the Tower.That Raistlin may be an ally they cannot control.
White Robe oppositionDemand oversight of forbidden research.That their earlier rigidity helped create the Black Master.
Dragonarmy IntelligenceOfficially nonexistent in the city.That Raistlin is developing a weapon capable of changing the war.
Cult of TakhisisHidden religious cell.That the Portal can be turned against the Queen.
Shoikan GroveNo human policy.It is waiting for the Master named in its curse.
FistandantilusNot yet recognised as an active faction.That Raistlin will choose love without possession and abandon the work.

pages.name: The Long Return: Clue Matrix
pages.html:
The Long Return should emerge as a theory in pieces. Do not hand the party a complete ritual until Arc IV.

ComponentWhat Conventional Resurrection DoesFistandantilus’s QuestionArc III Evidence
FleshRepairs or recreates a viable body.Can a vessel be rebuilt after centuries?Necromantic Vault; restored bodies.
SoulCalls a reachable spirit.Can an unreachable/displaced soul be located?Portal theory; Silvanesti notes.
MemoryAssumes identity returns with soul.Can reality’s memory reconstruct what death erased?Chamber of Echoes; Long Return fragments.
WillMost true resurrection permits refusal.Can refusal be removed?Necromantic Vault obedience; final missing section.

Fistandantilus’s most dangerous discovery is not resurrection. It is treating Will as a technical defect in the ritual.

pages.name: Shoikan Grove: GM Guide
pages.html:
The Grove is not a forest encounter table. It is an ancient Black-Robe guardian system layered with Rannoch’s curse and centuries of trapped death.

Visual Language

Enormous oaks. Bark black as pitch. Wounds in the trunks leaking red sap. Pale, bone-like branches. Sparse grey leaves. No natural sunlight beneath the canopy. Faces appear in shadows. Footprints fill with blood. Hands press upward beneath damp soil.

Six Zones

ZoneExperiencePurpose
1 Gate of TerrorPure supernatural fearTests whether the party relies only on immunity and numbers
2 Path of RegretPast choices made uglierSeeds personal material and tracker consequences
3 Dead ClearingRemains/spirits of failed intrudersShows the cost of claiming the prophecy
4 Three RoadsPower, knowledge, sacrifice pathsChoice reveals motive, not correct route
5 Master’s RoadRefuses PCs directlyClarifies recognition belongs to Raistlin
6 Servants’ GateA subordinate entrance opensTower admits the Master’s agents, not masters

Protection

The black token functions as Raistlin’s campaign equivalent of a Nightjewel/protective signature. It does not make the Grove safe. It prevents the guardian system from treating the party as ordinary intruders while allowing psychic and historical manifestations to continue.

pages.name: Tower Structure & Campaign Adaptation
pages.html:
The Doom-spire is more than six hundred feet tall, hollow through its centre, with a spiral stair and thirty-three floors. The campaign uses twelve principal zones for playable clarity.

Exterior

In this pre-claim state, the once white-and-red Lore-spire is grey shot with black. Its minarets are broken and rust-coloured. Gold and silver gates have twisted into dull blackened metal. Windows are dark. The surviving fabric of Rannoch’s robe moves at the gate without wind.

Interior Geometry

The central stair has no railing and opens into a drop that runs down the Tower’s hollow heart. Landings lead to galleries, archives, old residences, museums, classrooms and laboratories. Many are empty because the Orders removed what they could before abandoning Palanthas.

Twelve Adventure Zones

  1. Hall of Silence
  2. Hall of the Three Moons
  3. Abandoned Conclave
  4. Apprentice Quarters
  5. Forbidden Library
  6. Chamber of Echoes
  7. Rannoch’s Sanctum
  8. Fistandantilus’s Laboratory
  9. Observatory of Time
  10. Necromantic Vault
  11. Lower Seals
  12. Great Laboratory and Portal

Campaign Divergence

Published history later has Raistlin claim this Tower after the War of the Lance. In this campaign, events are happening earlier because Caramon’s death and Wayreth’s choice altered Raistlin’s path. Preserve the old architecture and prophecy; let the timeline itself become part of the mystery.

pages.name: Tower Phenomena d12
pages.html:
Roll only when a quiet corridor needs meaning. Every phenomenon should tell the party something about the Tower, its curse, or its expected Master.

d12Phenomenon
1A door opens onto a room exactly as it looked before the Lost Battles, then closes on darkness.
2Three coloured lights orbit a landing; the black light follows the White Robe.
3Someone hears Caramon’s laugh without knowing whose voice it is.
4A library shelf is empty except for dust outlines of books removed centuries ago.
5The stair below appears to stretch for miles; looking up restores normal distance.
6A spectral apprentice recites a lesson and waits for a player to answer.
7A mirror briefly gives one PC Raistlin’s hourglass eyes.
8Ink writes the words not yet across an abandoned desk.
9A bell sounds from Wayreth, impossible across the continent.
10One PC’s shadow walks half a step ahead and turns a corner first.
11A map of the Tower labels a floor with the PC’s name.
12For one breath, the walls become polished black and the broken domes seem restored in blood-red stone—a glimpse of a possible future.

pages.name: Session 1: The Dead Wizard
pages.html:
Session 1 · Level 8 · 4 hours. Open Arc III with a murder that makes Fistandantilus’s presence practical rather than theoretical.

Opening Image

Pellan Marr, the Aesthetic researcher who promised the party a meeting, is found at dawn one street from the Shoikan boundary. His body is cold. The frost around it points in three different directions.

People in Play

  • Pellan Marr — victim
  • Senior Aesthetic Teren
  • Professor Caldra Venn
  • Palanthas watch captain
  • Veyrath observer

Session Sequence

1. Scene Examination

The corpse shows necromantic residue and temporal distortion. A magical signature resembles Raistlin’s casting style but is older than his birth.

2. Witnesses

Residents heard Pellan arguing with someone who had Raistlin’s voice. Nobody saw a second person.

3. Library Audit

Pellan borrowed texts on Rannoch, Fistandantilus and temporal anchors. One page has been cut out with impossible precision.

4. False Accusation

A Palanthas official suggests Raistlin killed a scholar from Wayreth. The party must decide what they publicly reveal.

What Can Be Learned

  • Temporal and necromantic effects were combined.
  • The signature resembles Raistlin but predates him.
  • Pellan had found the phrase “Long Return.”

Tracker Guidance

Fistandantilus Influence +1 automatically. Raistlin Trust +1 if the party informs him privately before the city can use the death politically; -1 if they conceal evidence from everyone including him without a plan.

End Beat

In Pellan’s room, the party finds a scrap: FLESH — SOUL — MEMORY — WILL. Only the first three are annotated.

Narrative Thread

Fistandantilus is no longer background lore. Someone or something has acted in the present using his magical vocabulary.

pages.name: Session 2: The Lost Records
pages.html:
Session 2 · Level 8 · 3–4 hours. Turn Palanthas into an investigative map and let players choose how to pursue the Long Return.

Opening Image

Four institutions hold four incomplete versions of the same history, and each believes its copy is the reliable one.

People in Play

  • Astinus/Aesthetics
  • Professor Caldra Venn
  • White Robe archivist
  • Old City antiquarian
  • Harbour fence

Session Sequence

1. Choose Leads

Offer university archive, Aesthetic vault, noble collection and an Old City wizard estate. Each reveals a different component.

2. Contradictions

Dates disagree by days in documents that should be exact. The discrepancies line up with historical Night of the Eye events.

3. The Missing Name

Several records refer to a “living anchor” but the proper name has been removed from all copies.

4. Veyrath Pressure

A rival team steals a decoy record. If the party anticipated them, they can feed Veyrath a false destination.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Long Return is Fistandantilus’s theory of restoring the ancient dead.
  • It divides identity into Flesh, Soul, Memory and Will.
  • The Will section is missing from every accessible copy.

Tracker Guidance

Fistandantilus Influence +1 if the party follows clues exactly as laid without questioning their convenience. Trust +1 for feeding Veyrath false but plausible intelligence.

End Beat

The oldest map marks a sealed residence beneath the Old City as belonging to a Black Robe who corresponded with Fistandantilus.

Narrative Thread

The mystery becomes a scavenger trail designed by someone centuries ago. The party should begin asking who expected them to follow it.

pages.name: Session 3: Under the Old City
pages.html:
Session 3 · Level 8 · 4 hours. Recover the first substantial Long Return fragment and expose a physical route beneath Palanthas toward the Grove.

Opening Image

Beneath a wine cellar is masonry older than the street above it. The air smells of dust and old spell components rather than sewer water.

People in Play

  • Old City antiquarian
  • Spectral household servant
  • Dragonarmy infiltrators
  • Black Robe historical echo

Session Sequence

1. Hidden Residence

Explore a pre-Cataclysm wizard dwelling with intact study wards, domestic rooms and a collapsed tunnel leading toward the Tower district.

2. Correspondence

Letters show Fistandantilus requesting research on memory after death, not merely animation or resurrection.

3. Ambush

Veyrath’s cell arrives through a second entrance. Give the party a chance to negotiate, trap, misdirect or fight them.

4. The Fragment

A metal folio survives: Memory can be rebuilt from imprints left in places, objects and people. Caramon’s sword motif gains retrospective meaning, though the party may not know why.

What Can Be Learned

  • Memory is a recoverable magical component.
  • Fistandantilus researched emotional objects as anchors.
  • A service tunnel once connected this quarter to Tower support structures.

Tracker Guidance

Raistlin Trust +1 if the fragment reaches him intact. Control -1 if the party spares/captures infiltrators despite inconvenience; +1 only for gratuitous domination, not ordinary combat.

End Beat

The old tunnel ends at roots: black, wet, living roots of the Shoikan Grove pushing through stone.

Narrative Thread

The investigation now physically joins the city to the Grove. Session 4 crosses that boundary.

pages.name: Session 4: Gate of Terror
pages.html:
Session 4 · Level 8 · 4 hours. Enter the Shoikan Grove as a psychological dungeon rather than a simple combat zone.

Opening Image

The token protects the party from immediate annihilation, not from knowing what the Grove is designed to make them feel.

People in Play

  • Party
  • Shoikan dead
  • Personal memory manifestations
  • Distant Rannoch

Session Sequence

1. Gate of Terror

Each PC experiences their deepest current fear. Tie at least one vision to a tracker choice already made rather than a generic phobia.

2. Path of Regret

Replay one Arc I/II decision with consequences exaggerated until the players question whether the outcome was worth it.

3. Dead Clearing

Failed intruders remain as bones, spectres and objects. One carries the badge of a wizard school that still exists.

4. Shelter

The token creates a small still point where the party can short rest. On its surface, a glyph has appeared that was not there outside.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Grove responds to identity and authority.
  • Previous powerful wizards failed here.
  • Rannoch’s curse did not create the Grove but weaponised death within it.

Tracker Guidance

White Robe Bond +1 if the PC acknowledges a real past failure without surrendering judgment; no movement for simply “passing” fear. Wayreth Accord +1 for treating guardian magic as communicative.

End Beat

Three paths open ahead, each marked by a single word in Magius: POWER, KNOWLEDGE, SACRIFICE.

Narrative Thread

The Grove tests motive. All roads can ultimately work; the choice changes what it shows them.

pages.name: Session 5: The Servants’ Gate
pages.html:
Session 5 · Level 8 · 4 hours. Complete the Grove and establish the party’s subordinate relationship to the prophesied Master.

Opening Image

Whichever road the party chose, it ends at the same black wall—but at a different emotional cost.

People in Play

  • Party
  • Rannoch echo
  • Tower guardian
  • Grove manifestations

Session Sequence

1. Three Roads Resolution

Power offers a shortcut requiring domination of a spirit. Knowledge offers a riddle that reveals a dangerous truth. Sacrifice demands a real resource or memory be relinquished temporarily. Do not label one morally correct.

2. Master’s Road

A straight road to the main gate appears and then refuses them. The token burns cold. A message forms: Not the Master.

3. Subordinate Route

An older service path opens around the wall to a servants’ gate. This gate recognises the token and the party’s role.

4. Entry

The door opens into absolute silence. The Grove closes behind them. For the first time in centuries, living people stand inside the Doom-spire without the Master present.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Tower distinguishes Master from agents.
  • Raistlin’s recognition is specific, not transferable.
  • The party has a legitimate subordinate entrance while the main gate remains cursed.

Tracker Guidance

Wayreth Accord +1–2 if the party solved the Grove without attempting to force the Master’s Road. Raistlin Control shifts according to the road solution, not road choice.

End Beat

The inner door closes. Their footsteps make no echo.

Narrative Thread

Raistlin has not entered yet. The party must discover enough truth to understand what his arrival will mean.

pages.name: Session 6: Hall of Silence & Three Moons
pages.html:
Session 6 · Level 8–9 · 4 hours. Introduce Tower scale, activate the three-moon machinery, and make the party feel observed by an artifact built for all Orders.

Opening Image

The central hall is hollow from base to impossible height. A stair without railing spirals upward around open air. Dust lies everywhere except on one narrow path ahead.

People in Play

  • Party
  • Invisible servant echoes
  • Three-moon orrery
  • Optional spectral instructor

Session Sequence

1. Hall of Silence

Explore abandoned receiving rooms, stripped display cases and service passages. Sounds die unnaturally; doors close softly by themselves.

2. Restore Access

A ward nexus must be powered by three distinct magical principles—protection, transformation and destructive command—mirroring the Orders without demanding matching PCs.

3. Hall of Three Moons

Three enormous mechanisms represent Solinari, Lunitari and Nuitari. The White Robe activates Solinari. Other arcane PCs may trigger different responses.

4. Unexpected Response

When Raistlin’s token is placed near the central mechanism, all three orreries move one fraction of a turn, then stop.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Tower was built for cooperation among all Orders.
  • Its systems recognise Order affiliations.
  • Raistlin’s signature produces a response across all three moon mechanisms.

Tracker Guidance

Wayreth Accord +1 for collaborative solution. Fistandantilus Influence +1 only if the party interprets the all-three response as proof of destiny rather than evidence requiring caution.

End Beat

A stair segment rotates into place, opening the route toward the old Conclave rooms.

Narrative Thread

The all-three response previews Raistlin’s final arrival without giving him the scene yet.

pages.name: Session 7: The Abandoned Conclave
pages.html:
Session 7 · Level 9 · 4 hours. Teach the Lost Battles as experienced political memory and show how institutional fear can become cruelty.

Opening Image

The council chamber is intact. Twenty-one seats remain. When the party enters, spectral occupants appear and continue a debate abandoned centuries ago.

People in Play

  • Echoes of Conclave members
  • Highmage Merroc echo
  • Rannoch in earlier life
  • Projected Knights/Kingpriest envoys

Session Sequence

1. Living Debate

Players can ask questions and be answered as though they are delegates from the past. The echoes cannot perceive modern names reliably.

2. Lost Battles

The chamber reenacts evacuation arguments, Tower destruction, artefact removal and the fear of the Portal falling into hostile hands.

3. Andras

Show him first as a manipulated, grieving wizard rather than a gate spectre. Fistandantilus repeatedly offers him “one more necessary act.”

4. Vote

The party is asked to cast symbolic votes on whether to destroy knowledge to keep it from enemies. Their vote cannot change history but changes what memory unlocks.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Orders destroyed their own Towers rather than surrender them.
  • Fistandantilus manipulated Andras before the curse.
  • The Portal was moved away from Palanthas before Fistandantilus sought it.

Tracker Guidance

White Robe Bond +1 if the PC can critique the White/Conclave decisions without pretending there was an easy alternative. Control shifts if the party frames destruction or domination as automatic solutions.

End Beat

The final echo says: “The apprentices must be evacuated.” A door to their quarters opens.

Narrative Thread

The arc’s institutional theme matters because Raistlin’s break with the White Robes must feel like a reaction to real failures, not simple villainy.

pages.name: Session 8: The Apprentice Quarters
pages.html:
Session 8 · Level 9 · 3–4 hours. Humanise the ancient Tower and confront the party with young dead who never became legendary archmages.

Opening Image

Dormitories still contain half-packed trunks. A slate has tomorrow’s lessons written on it. Tomorrow never happened.

People in Play

  • Sane apprentice spirits
  • Hostile repetitive spirits
  • One spirit who recognises the White Robe as “late”
  • Invisible servants

Session Sequence

1. Dormitory Life

Let players find letters home, failed exercises, petty rivalries and mundane chores. The old Orders become people.

2. The Lesson Repeats

A classroom cycles through a lesson on ethical summoning. Breaking the loop requires answering why a summoned creature’s consent matters.

3. The Late Student

A spirit addresses the White Robe: “You are late.” It believes the current candidate was expected generations ago.

4. Release or Use

The party can free spirits by completing evacuation rites, or compel them for information. Both work; one is faster.

What Can Be Learned

  • Consent was debated inside old magical curricula, not invented by the current party.
  • Some dead have been trapped by the curse rather than choice.
  • The phrase “late” suggests temporal expectation inside the Tower.

Tracker Guidance

Raistlin Control -1 for freeing spirits at meaningful cost; +1 if they compel them when a viable release route is known. White Robe Bond can rise through compassion with responsibility.

End Beat

A freed apprentice points toward a sealed library door and says, “He hid the ugly books where all of us could see the lock.”

Narrative Thread

The Will component of the Long Return is being foreshadowed through small acts before the ritual is explicit.

pages.name: Session 9: The Forbidden Library
pages.html:
Session 9 · Level 9–10 · 4 hours. Recover the first substantial Long Return text and make dangerous knowledge genuinely useful.

Opening Image

The library door is covered with warnings in three different hands. One warning says simply: Do not burn what frightens you. Understand it first.

People in Play

  • Party
  • Archive ward
  • Fistandantilus textual echo
  • Optional Veyrath infiltrator separated from team

Session Sequence

1. Ward of Classification

The lock opens only if books are sorted by consequence rather than school: destructive, coercive, transformative, restorative, planar.

2. Research

Find necromancy, soul theory, chronomancy, planar binding, Dragon Orb material and Fistandantilus fragments.

3. The Long Return

Recover sections proving that Memory can be reconstructed and that a distant soul may be reached through a Portal/anchor combination.

4. Intruder

A lone enemy scholar can be captured. They reveal Veyrath’s cell followed the party through the Grove using the briefly opened path, not Raistlin’s token.

What Can Be Learned

  • Fistandantilus separated resurrection into components.
  • A living emotional anchor can make an otherwise unreachable soul locatable.
  • The missing Will section was removed deliberately, not lost by accident.

Tracker Guidance

Level 10 if pacing needs a mid-arc milestone; otherwise award at Session 10. Fistandantilus Influence +1 for using his framework; Control does not move merely for researching dark magic.

End Beat

A hidden catalogue references a chamber capable of replaying the memories of the Tower’s recognised Master.

Narrative Thread

The library establishes the campaign’s rule: forbidden knowledge is not automatically evil. The choices made with it are what matter.

pages.name: Session 10: The Chamber of Echoes
pages.html:
Session 10 · Level 10 · 4–5 hours. Reveal Caramon’s death and the Garden Incident, converting Raistlin from enigmatic patron into the emotional centre of the campaign.

Opening Image

The chamber activates from Raistlin’s token. It does not show historical Tower memories. It shows the memories the Tower associates with its current Master.

People in Play

  • Raistlin memory echo
  • Caramon memory echo
  • Par-Salian memory echo
  • White/Red/Black Order witnesses in memories

Session Sequence

1. Silvanesti

Show Caramon’s death inside Lorac’s Nightmare and Raistlin surviving. Do not rush. The sword from the Master’s chamber is visible in Caramon’s hand.

2. Search

Raistlin combs the nightmare for his brother, attempts conventional resurrection, seeks specialists and gets the same answer: the soul is unreachable.

3. Refusal

The White Robes confiscate temporal/necromantic research and Par-Salian blocks access. Make their reasons understandable and their method cold.

4. Red to Black

Raistlin takes the Black not as theatrical corruption but because the Black Order will let him continue.

5. Garden Incident

Par-Salian takes his customary walk. Wayreth refuses to let him return. Paths loop. Teleportation places him at the garden gate. At the same hour the Forest opens for Raistlin, gates unlock, stairs move, lights awaken, the Master’s chambers open, and the wards record one word: MASTER.

What Can Be Learned

  • Caramon is dead in this timeline.
  • Raistlin’s entire research programme began as an attempt to retrieve him.
  • Wayreth chose Raistlin before the Conclave ratified him.
  • The Tower chose survival probability, not moral virtue.

Tracker Guidance

Level 10. Raistlin Trust +1 if the party later tells him they saw this rather than hiding it; White Robe Bond may shift ±2 depending on whether the PC responds with compassion plus limits or mere condemnation. Fistandantilus Influence unchanged: this is Raistlin’s grief, not the Dark One’s philosophy yet.

End Beat

The final memory freezes on Raistlin seated in the Master’s chamber beneath Caramon’s sword. A new door opens behind the image.

Narrative Thread

This is the reveal the first two arcs have been building toward. From here onward, every ethical choice must be understood against the fact that Raistlin’s original desire is painfully human.

pages.name: Session 11: Rannoch’s Sanctum
pages.html:
Session 11 · Level 10 · 4 hours. Confront Andras Rannoch as both guardian and victim of Fistandantilus’s long plan.

Opening Image

The sanctum is built around a vertical shaft facing the gates below. Rannoch’s spirit is strongest here, where every version of his death overlaps.

People in Play

  • Spectre/echo of Andras Rannoch
  • Memories of Fistandantilus
  • Guardian dead

Session Sequence

1. Accusation

Rannoch calls the party servants of the next Dark One. He believes Raistlin is not escaping Fistandantilus’s pattern but fulfilling it early.

2. His History

Through argument or memory fragments, learn that Fistandantilus rescued, taught and weaponised Andras until grief and vengeance made him useful.

3. Choice

Defeat, persuade or release him. Release requires acknowledging his guilt without pretending manipulation erases responsibility.

4. Curse Key

Rannoch reveals the curse’s condition was chosen with knowledge that a Master of Past and Present would eventually come.

What Can Be Learned

  • Fistandantilus planned for a future Master.
  • Andras acted as Fistandantilus’s instrument in establishing the curse.
  • The prophecy is engineered as well as mystical.

Tracker Guidance

Fistandantilus Influence +1. Raistlin Control -1 for releasing Rannoch through responsibility/consent; +1 if the party permanently binds him for convenience. Wayreth Accord +1 if released.

End Beat

Rannoch names a laboratory one level below that belonged to “the Dark One before he had a face here.”

Narrative Thread

The party should now suspect the prophecy may be a trap built to look like destiny.

pages.name: Session 12: Fistandantilus’s Laboratory
pages.html:
Session 12 · Level 10–11 · 4 hours. Make the Dark One’s long preparation undeniable and blur the line between prediction, time, and manipulation.

Opening Image

Some papers are brittle with centuries. Others smell of fresh ink. Several lines are in Raistlin’s hand. Several more are in Fistandantilus’s, and there are places where no one at the table can tell which is which.

People in Play

  • Fistandantilus textual/illusion echo
  • Arcane simulacra
  • Party

Session Sequence

1. Impossible Documents

Date papers across centuries. One references “the golden-skinned heir” before Raistlin’s birth. Another describes a powerful twin without naming Caramon.

2. Handwriting Test

Allow magical and mundane analysis. The scripts are distinct at first and converge around passages about Will and possession.

3. Prepared Trail

A sequence of sealed drawers opens only to spells/phrases the party learned in earlier clues, proving the trail expected a future reader.

4. The Missing Work

The final drawer is empty except for a map to three sites: Silvanesti, Zhaman, Istar. These become Arc IV.

What Can Be Learned

  • Fistandantilus expected a successor fitting Raistlin’s circumstances.
  • Three physical research components are missing.
  • The final unresolved problem is Will.

Tracker Guidance

Level 11 if not already. Fistandantilus Influence +2. Raistlin Trust depends on whether the party reports the “golden-skinned heir” language honestly.

End Beat

One page writes a new line while the party watches: You are closer than he was.

Narrative Thread

Fistandantilus is now acting across the line between record and present. Do not yet have him speak directly; save direct manifestation for Arc VI.

pages.name: Session 13: Observatory of Time
pages.html:
Session 13 · Level 11 · 4 hours. Show possible futures without declaring a canonical answer and let players see their own effect on Raistlin.

Opening Image

The observatory dome has no visible sky. Instead, six futures occupy six wedges of the room like windows that can be walked into.

People in Play

  • Possible Raistlins
  • Possible White Robe
  • Possible party members
  • Caramon in several states

Session Sequence

1. Future One

Raistlin defeats Takhisis and remains mortal. The Orders survive, changed.

2. Future Two

Raistlin rules Krynn as an authoritarian archmage. The war is over. The streets are safe.

3. Future Three

Raistlin becomes a god above a dead world.

4. Future Four

Raistlin sacrifices himself and the Towers outlive him.

5. Future Five

The White Robe kills Raistlin before the Portal opens; the consequences are not all good.

6. Future Six

Raistlin and the White Robe stand together before the Portal, arguing while everything depends on the argument.

What Can Be Learned

  • None of the futures is marked true.
  • The party’s presence changes probabilities inside several visions.
  • Wayreth’s original choice can be understood as probability without morality.

Tracker Guidance

Wayreth Accord +1–2 if the party grasps the Tower’s survival logic without treating a vision as instruction. White Robe Bond +1 if the PC refuses the premise that only killing or obeying Raistlin are options.

End Beat

The visions collapse to one image: a vault containing people who should be dead.

Narrative Thread

The finale is not predetermined. The tracker board measures relationships and habits, not a hidden “correct ending.”

pages.name: Session 14: The Necromantic Vault
pages.html:
Session 14 · Level 11 · 4 hours. Prove Fistandantilus could restore the dead and reveal the obedience flaw at the heart of his method.

Opening Image

The first restored person looks alive. They breathe, shiver, remember their name, and ask what year it is.

People in Play

  • Restored experimental subjects
  • Vault wardens
  • Fistandantilus recorded instructions

Session Sequence

1. The Living Dead

Do not use zombie aesthetics. Subjects have memories, personalities and fear. Some are centuries displaced.

2. Command Reflex

When a Fistandantilus instruction is spoken, every restored subject obeys before consciously deciding to.

3. Ethical Problem

One subject begs the party to destroy the command lattice even if doing so may kill them. Another refuses because they want to live.

4. Technical Proof

The ritual successfully rebuilt Flesh, called Soul and reconstructed Memory. The Will component was replaced by obedience.

What Can Be Learned

  • The Long Return works.
  • Fistandantilus’s version binds Will.
  • Restoration and enslavement can be technically inseparable if the ritual is not changed.

Tracker Guidance

Raistlin Control ±2 based on the party’s handling of the subjects and what they recommend to Raistlin. White Robe Bond +1 for a solution that respects conflicting wishes rather than imposing one group answer.

End Beat

The vault’s lower seal opens only after the command lattice is resolved. Something on the far side is already trying to come through.

Narrative Thread

This is the first proof that Raistlin’s dream is possible and therefore the first real temptation to excuse the flaw.

pages.name: Session 15: The Lower Seals
pages.html:
Session 15 · Level 11 · 4–5 hours. Turn the final descent into simultaneous dungeon defense and intelligence conflict.

Opening Image

The air below the vault moves inward toward the Portal chamber, as if the Tower is breathing. The seal wards are failing in a pattern that is not natural decay.

People in Play

  • Veyrath or his elite agents
  • Cult of Takhisis cell
  • Planar anomalies
  • Ancient arcane guardians

Session Sequence

1. Breach Map

Three seals fail at different depths. The party must decide order while enemy agents enter through a route opened during earlier Grove disturbances.

2. Enemy Objective

Veyrath wants evidence; the cult wants the Portal damaged or claimed. Their goals conflict, giving the party leverage.

3. Planar Guardians

Creatures appear only partially in the world. Use environmental effects and short combats rather than a single boss.

4. Veyrath Resolution

Give the party a chance to finally defeat Veyrath strategically: expose his network, turn him, capture him, or force him to retreat with the wrong conclusion.

What Can Be Learned

  • Takhisis’s servants know a Portal exists.
  • The Portal is not simply a gate; it can affect souls across planar boundaries.
  • Enemy high command will eventually act directly against both Towers.

Tracker Guidance

War State ±1 based on the intelligence outcome. Trust +1 for defending the mission without sacrificing Palanthas civilians. Control changes only for choices of binding/coercion.

End Beat

Beyond the final seal stands a black velvet curtain. Behind it, something that is not wind moves the fabric.

Narrative Thread

The Portal chamber is the hinge between private grief and world war. Arc III ends when Raistlin comes to see it himself.

pages.name: Session 16: The Master Arrives
pages.html:
Session 16 · Level 12 · 4–5 hours. Pay off three arcs of prophecy by letting Raistlin claim recognition without yet opening the Portal.

Opening Image

Palanthas gathers to watch because word has spread that Raistlin Majere is walking toward the Shoikan Grove. He comes alone.

People in Play

  • Raistlin Majere
  • Party
  • Palanthas citizens
  • Astinus observers
  • Order representatives
  • Shoikan guardians
  • Tower itself

Session Sequence

1. The Walk

Raistlin approaches the Grove. Terror vanishes before him. Trees bow away. He casts no spell.

2. The Gate

The main gates, which refused the party, open. Rannoch’s remaining manifestation either bows, is silent, or is absent depending on Session 11.

3. Hall of Three Moons

As Raistlin enters, Solinari, Lunitari and Nuitari mechanisms ignite together: white, red, black.

4. The Name

Wards throughout the Tower identify him: RAISTLIN MAJERE — MASTER OF PAST AND PRESENT.

5. The Portal

He reaches the Great Laboratory. The Portal remains dormant. He studies it, then says only: “Not yet.”

6. The Next Errand

He explains that three components of Fistandantilus’s work are missing and must be recovered from Silvanesti, Zhaman and Istar.

What Can Be Learned

  • The prophecy has been fulfilled early in this altered timeline.
  • Raistlin now has legitimate supernatural authority over both Wayreth and Palanthas.
  • He still chooses not to open the Portal without understanding the ritual.

Tracker Guidance

Level 12. Wayreth Accord +1 if the party helped release/repair Tower systems. Fistandantilus Influence +1 automatically. White Robe Bond may rise if Raistlin deliberately seeks their opinion before declaring the next mission.

End Beat

As the party leaves the Great Laboratory, the Portal’s dark surface reflects four people: Raistlin, the White Robe, one PC—and Caramon.

Narrative Thread

Arc III ends not with Raistlin becoming more evil, but with his impossible hope becoming technically achievable. Arc IV asks what the price really is.
